ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $ \angle AOB = 120^\circ$ and $ \angle BOC = 30^\circ$. If $OD$ is the angle bisector of $ \angle AOC$, find the measure of $ \angle BOD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because \angle AOB=120^\circ$ and $\angle BOC=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOC=\angle AOB - \angle BOC=90^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because$ OD is the bisector of $\angle AOC$,\\
$\therefore \angle COD=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOD=\angle COD+\angle BOC =45^\circ+30^\circ=\boxed{75^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, four rays are drawn with O as the common endpoint. Ray OA extends from O upward and slightly to the right, ray OD points to the upper right, ray OC points to the lower right and slightly upward, and ray OB points to the lower right and slightly downward. From the figure, the order of the rays around point O is A, D, C, B; therefore ∠AOC is the part remaining after removing ∠BOC from ∠AOB, while ∠BOD is composed of the two parts ∠BOC and ∠COD. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOB = 120°, ∠BOC = 30°, so ∠AOC = ∠AOB - ∠BOC = 120° - 30° = 90°. Also because OD is the angle bisector of ∠AOC, ∠COD = 1/2 × ∠AOC = 45°. Therefore ∠BOD = ∠BOC + ∠COD = 30° + 45° = 75°.
